title: Reading the GRPO equation, line by line
summary: Open the GRPO objective from the DeepSeekMath paper and translate every symbol into plain words and a line of the Tiny Adder code. Then see exactly which pieces DAPO and Dr. GRPO changed, and why.
learningObjectives: Read each symbol of the GRPO objective aloud in plain words
Map every part of the equation to a line of grpo_tiny_adder.py
Explain how GRPO's per-token KL estimator works and why it is always non-negative
Explain the length bias of the 1/|o_i| average and how Dr. GRPO and DAPO change it
concepts: policy, old policy and reference policy

studyGuide.mentalModel: The equation is a recipe written in shorthand: average over questions and their sampled groups; inside, average over answers and over tokens; for each token, take the clipped ratio times the group-relative advantage; subtract beta times a KL estimate; then climb uphill. Every line has a twin in the Tiny Adder code.
keyIdeas: E over q and {o_i} ~ pi_old means: sample questions and a group of G answers each from the model that is about to be updated.
(1/G) sum over i averages over the group; (1/|o_i|) sum over t averages over the tokens of one answer.
With outcome rewards, every token of an answer shares the same advantage (r_i - mean) / std.
GRPO subtracts beta times a per-token KL estimate, pi_ref/pi - log(pi_ref/pi) - 1, which is never negative.
Dr. GRPO and DAPO change the length average and the std division; TRL exposes them as loss_type and scale_rewards.
misconceptions: pi_old is not the reference model: pi_old sampled the current batch, pi_ref is frozen from the start.
The KL term in GRPO is not added to the reward as in classic RLHF PPO; it is a separate term in the loss.
Dividing by answer length is not neutral: it weakens the per-token penalty on long wrong answers.
The changes in DAPO and Dr. GRPO do not replace GRPO's core idea; groups and relative advantages stay.
recallPrompts: What is the difference between pi_theta, pi_theta_old and pi_ref?
Why does the token average do nothing in Tiny Adder?
Write the k3 KL estimate in words. What is it when the two probabilities are equal?
Which TRL setting chooses between the original GRPO, DAPO and Dr. GRPO loss aggregation?
studyGuide.explainBackPrompt: Explain to a friend what each part of the GRPO equation instructs the computer to do, using the Tiny Adder as the example, and name one part that later research changed.

quiz.prompt: In the GRPO equation, what is the difference between pi_theta_old and pi_ref?
options: They are two names for the same model
pi_theta_old is a bigger teacher model; pi_ref is the student
pi_ref is updated every step; pi_theta_old never changes
pi_theta_old is the model that sampled the current batch; pi_ref is the frozen starting model used for the KL penalty
quiz.explanation: The ratio compares against pi_theta_old (a moment ago), which is what clipping uses. The KL term compares against pi_ref (frozen at the start).

quiz.prompt: With outcome supervision (one reward per complete answer), what advantage does each token of answer o_i get?
options: The same value for every token: (r_i - group mean) / group std
A different value per token, from a critic network
Zero for all tokens except the last one
quiz.explanation: Every token of an answer shares the answer's group-normalized reward. Process supervision, a variant in the paper, gives per-step rewards instead.

quiz.prompt: GRPO estimates KL per token as pi_ref/pi_theta - log(pi_ref/pi_theta) - 1. What is this estimate when pi_ref and pi_theta give the token the same probability?
quiz.explanation: The ratio is 1, log(1) = 0, so 1 - 0 - 1 = 0. The estimate is never negative and grows as the two models disagree.

quiz.prompt: Why does the 1/|o_i| average in the original GRPO loss create a length bias?
options: It makes long answers impossible to sample
It spreads each answer's advantage over its tokens, so long wrong answers get a weaker per-token penalty than short wrong ones
It doubles the reward of long answers
It removes the KL penalty for long answers
quiz.explanation: An advantage of -1 over 200 tokens is -0.005 per token, versus -0.02 over 50 tokens. Dr. GRPO and DAPO change this aggregation.

quiz.prompt: Why does the (1/|o_i|) sum over t part of the equation do nothing in Tiny Adder?
options: Because Tiny Adder has no reward
Because each Tiny Adder answer is a single token, so |o_i| = 1
quiz.explanation: An answer is one number, so averaging over its tokens averages over exactly one value.
